subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core add a first-class updater workflow, and what approval, scheduling, channel-targeting, and post-restart reporting contract should it expose?
rationale: The remaining work affects package replacement, unattended updates, operator consent, persisted restart state, and cross-channel notifications, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent config, security, and UX boundary.

options.title: Design core workflow on safe updater path
options.body: Define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and update.run or external-updater execution boundary before implementation.

options.title: Keep package auto-updater only
options.body: Leave update.auto as rollout/cadence policy and route confirmation or notification orchestration to user cron, agents, or plugins until a stronger core need is confirmed.

options.title: Split narrower follow-ups
options.body: Track post-update hooks, UI discoverability, safe rollback, skill/plugin auto-update, and external-updater mechanics separately while keeping this issue as the workflow umbrella.

recommendation.title: Design core workflow on safe updater path
recommendation.body: Define the opt-in config, approval modes, notification routing, restart-state persistence, and update.run or external-updater execution boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the core package auto-updater and has already reviewed this as the canonical workflow gap.
